question: What did the Chicago Bears' 73–0 win in the 1940 NFL Championship game do to American football formations?
answer: It made the T-formation standard. The Bears set their quarterback directly behind the centre and sent a back running sideways before the snap, a man in motion, hiding where the play would go. Washington had beaten them weeks earlier. Within about a decade almost every professional and college team ran some version of the T.
move: One lopsided result can convert a field faster than years of argument.
reference: Peterson, Pigskin: The Early Years of Pro Football, Oxford University Press, 1997
